title: Hong Kong Open: Race to Finals Down to the Wire
article_text:
The LI-NING Hong Kong Open 2026 marks the final stop on the HSBC Race to Finals, with the last available points on offer before the HSBC BWF World Tour Finals in Hangzhou next month.

While several berths have already been secured, a handful of coveted spots remain up for grabs across the disciplines, setting the stage for a high-stakes week in Hong Kong.

Among the biggest beneficiaries of late developments is Anders Antonsen. The Dane received a timely boost from the Seed Withdrawal Movement, which elevated him to the No.1 position in the draw in place of top seed Christo Popov. The promotion comes with a first-round bye and, crucially, enough ranking points to mathematically secure his place in Hangzhou.

Not everyone has enjoyed such a fortunate turn; Chinese Taipei’s Chou Tien Chen faces a sterner challenge than originally expected. Scheduled to meet Nhat Nguyen, Chou will instead open against fast-rising Indonesian Moh. Zaki Ubaidillah.

The race could also be influenced by events elsewhere. Following the withdrawal of his original opponent Alwi Farhan, India’s Kidambi Srikanth has an opportunity to help compatriot Lakshya Sen’s hopes when he takes on Koki Watanabe. A Watanabe defeat would secure qualification for Sen, Chou and Kunlavut Vitidsarn, making the first round clash one of the most significant of the week.

The drama is equally intense in the doubles disciplines. In both men’s and women’s doubles, six pairs are vying for four remaining spots, with all contenders present in Hong Kong.

Among those hoping to make history are Lauren Lam and Allison Lee. The duo are chasing a breakthrough qualification that would see them become the first Americans in any doubles discipline to reach a season finale.

With Hangzhou beckoning, the final chapter of the HSBC Race to Finals promises tension, twists and no shortage of drama.

LI-NING Hong Kong Open 2026 begins today, with the first qualification match scheduled for 9am Kuala Lumpur time (UTC +8).

title: BWF World Ranking: Sindhu Rises To No.5, Lakshya To No.11
article_text:
BWF World Ranking: Sindhu Rises To No.5, Lakshya To No.11

PV Sindhu moves up to world No.5, and Lakshya Sen rises two places to No.11 in the BWF World Rankings in the singles event as the World Tour Finals near.

Indian aces PV Sindhu and Lakshya Sen have moved up in their latest BWF World Rankings. Sindhu has climbed one place to World No.5 in the BWF women’s singles rankings, and Lakshya has climbed two places to No. 11 in the BWF men’s singles rankings. The progress happened after Sen won the Hylo Open and the Kumamoto Masters Japan in two successive weeks, and Sindhu won the Hylo Open 2026. Additionally, Sindhu has already qualified for the World Tour Finals in December, while Lakshya is still in the race for the badminton final tour. In women's doubles, Arjuna Award winners Tressa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand Pullela are currently ranked 19th in the world rankings. The World Championships bronze medallist achieved the highest rank of No.9 in January 2025.

Sindhu was sixth in the badminton rankings on 10 November, so this is her second rise in two weeks. She is also fifth in the World Tour rankings for women’s singles.

Lakshya has beaten Alwi Farhan and Koki Watanabe on his way to the Kumamoto title. He is 5,566 points behind Farhan, who is in tenth.

Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand are 19th with 53,022 points, up one place. They are well behind the fifth-placed Iwanaga and Nakanishi, the Japanese pair who beat them in the Kumamoto Masters Round of 16.

Lakshya won the Kumamoto Masters Japan 2026 title, beating Koki Watanabe 13-21, 21-18, 21-14 in the final. It was his second straight Super 500 title, after the Hylo Open. He is also sixth in the Race to the BWF World Tour Finals, which begins on 9 December in China.

title: Teenager Mirra Andreeva joins elite group of tennis stars after winning WTA Finals without losing a singl
article_text:
NEW DELHI: Russian tennis star Mirra Andreeva capped off a remarkable season by winning the WTA Finals without losing a single set. The 19-year-old defeated Ukraine's Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 in Sunday's final to finish the tournament with five wins from five matches.

The victory also helped Andreeva reach a career-best world ranking of No. 2, behind Kazakhstan's Elena Rybakina.

Along with the title, Andreeva earned $3.37 million in prize money and a unique ultraviolet purple Mercedes-Benz convertible. However, there is one thing she still needs before she can drive her new car: a driver's license.

“This is an amazing motivation for me to get my driver's license as fast as I can,” she said. “If not, then look, I have five people on my team. I'm going to be a passenger's princess forever, that's also an option for me.”

With this victory, Andreeva became only the 11th player to win the WTA Finals without dropping a set. She joined legendary names such as Chris Evert, Martina Navratilova and Serena Williams.

Speaking after her win, the teenager expressed her happiness at joining such an elite group.

“I'm super privileged to put my name in that group,” she said.

Andreeva also took a moment to appreciate her own hard work during the awards ceremony. Wearing a jacket with the words 'I want to thank myself', she spoke about the effort and dedication behind her success.

“I want to thank myself for always doing the hard work, for never quitting, for always believing in myself, for not taking the days off, for working every day and for committing to what I have to do,” she said. “Just thanks to myself without any reason.”

The final was closely fought, with both players exchanging breaks and battling hard from the baseline. However, Andreeva won five of the last six games to seal the title in just under two hours.

The match ended after Svitolina missed an easy smash, giving Andreeva the victory. The players did not shake hands after the match, continuing the practice followed by Ukrainian players against Russian and Belarusian opponents since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Despite the situation, Andreeva congratulated Svitolina on her season and praised her comeback as a mother.

“You're an amazing mom to come back and do this. It's super hard,” she said. “I just wish you the best of luck for the next season.”

Svitolina also acknowledged Andreeva's performance, saying, “I put everything out there and she played incredible.”

article_text:
INDIAN WELLS, Calif. -- Two years after falling one match short of the title at the WTA Finals, Katerina Siniakova and Taylor Townsend got another chance to lift the trophy. This time, they made it count, defeating Sara Errani and Jasmine Paolini 6-4, 6-3 on Sunday to capture their first FAGE WTA Finals title as a team and their sixth title of the season.

Siniakova and Townsend opened the week with a loss to the Italians in the group stage. Errani and Paolini, the last team to qualify for the season-ending tournament, had won all four of their matches en route to their first WTA Finals championship match. But the second seeds ended that unbeaten run on the same courts where they had won the Indian Wells title in March.

It was Townsend's first WTA Finals title and Siniakova's second, having previously won the championship with Barbora Krejcikova in 2021.

Errani and Paolini made a strong start, securing an early break to take a 3-1 lead in the opening set. But Siniakova and Townsend rallied from 4-2 down, winning four consecutive games to take the set 6-4.

The second set followed a similar pattern, with the Italians breaking serve to go ahead 2-1. However, they were unable to consolidate the break as Siniakova and Townsend broke straight back. The Czech-American duo secured another break in the eighth game before serving out the 6-4, 6-3 victory in 1 hour, 15 minutes.

Sunday's final marked the fourth meeting between the two teams this season. Although Errani and Paolini had won their group-stage encounter earlier in the week, Siniakova and Townsend had prevailed in their previous two meetings -- in the semifinals at Indian Wells and the final in Miami.

This was the third consecutive WTA Finals appearance as a team for Siniakova and Townsend, who finished runners-up in 2024 and reached the semifinals last year.

Errani and Paolini were also making their third consecutive appearance at the season-ending tournament, but this was the first time they had advanced beyond the group stage. Sunday's defeat snapped an eight-match winning streak for the Italians, who arrived in Indian Wells after winning the title in Tokyo.

Having already won titles together at Roland Garros, the US Open, Madrid, Miami and Indian Wells this season, Siniakova and Townsend added a sixth trophy to their collection. It was their ninth title as a team overall and marked Siniakova's 40th tour-level doubles title and Townsend's 18th.

Siniakova will also finish the season as the year-end World No. 1 in doubles for a record sixth time, surpassing Martina Navratilova's previous record of five year-end No. 1 finishes.

title: Fusion Racing confirms identity as 12th Formula E entry with Porsche supply
article_text:
The 2026-27 Formula E season is taking shape after multi-category motor racing organization Fusion announced its participation, becoming the 12th team on the grid for the all-electric series.

Fusion Formula E Team will be a Porsche factory team, meaning it will utilize the Porsche 975 RSE power train developed by the German manufacturer (which supplies two other Formula E entrants, including its own branded factory team).

Initially, Porsche had sought to field a second factory team after ending the participation of its Porsche Penske Motorsport team in the FIA World Endurance Championship, but instead it has opted to facilitate Fusion’s entry, serving as a supplier to the new team instead of a parent.

The Fusion entry will be led by Phil Charles, the former technical director and deputy team principal of the now-defunct DS Penske Formula E team, who will be supported by sporting director Chris Bluett, who was team manager at DS Penske. A driver lineup has yet to be confirmed.

Fusion has already tapped a number of organization-wide sponsors to partner the Formula E entry, including logistics company Metro Supply Chain, subscription management platform OpenByte, pet tagging brand Crumb, luxury vehicle dealer Automobiles Etcetera, and digital security firm TotalAV, all of which have featured on preliminary images of the Fusion Formula E car, as does Porsche as the power unit supplier.

These categories include Formula 2, Formula 3, the Formula Regional European Championship, and the domestic F4 series in Italy, Germany, and the UK, through its LN4 Racing arm.

title: Prendergast cited and could miss South Africa game
article_text:
Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast is in danger of missing Saturday's Nations Championship match against South Africa after being cited for a tackle against Fiji.

Prendergast will face a disciplinary process for a hip-drop tackle on Fijian captain Peceli Yato in the first half of Ireland's 43-15 win in Dublin on Saturday.

The technique, when a tackling player drops their hips and bodyweight on to the ball-carrier's legs, was outlawed by World Rugby before November's internationals and the 23-year-old is the first player to be cited over its use in a game.

If found guilty and he accepts the verdict, Prendergast could face a pre-determined sanction through the Six Nations' expedited disciplinary process.

However, if he does not accept the charge then he would be referred to a panel to determine any possible outcome.

Australia's Angus Bell was yellow carded for a hip-drop tackle against England, but Prendergast's alleged offence was not penalised by match officials during the match.

If Prendergast receives a suspension, Connacht fly-half Ciaran Frawley would be the prime candidate to start against the Springboks on Saturday [16:40 GMT].

Ulster's Jamie Benson, who has yet to be capped at international level, is also an option for Farrell.

In better news for Ireland, captain Dan Sheehan is set to return for the game against the back-to-back world champions at the Aviva Stadium after he completed return to play protocols.

Sheehan - who is deputising for regular skipper Caelan Doris - missed Saturday's win over Fiji after sustaining a concussion in the defeat of Argentina on 6 November.

But in a squad update issued on Monday, the Irish Rugby Football Union (IRFU) said Sheehan will return to full training this week before the Springboks' visit to Dublin.

Ulster back row James McNabney is unavailable while he undergoes 12-day return to play protocols after sustaining a head injury that prematurely ended his eye-catching debut off the bench against the Fijians.

Tight-head prop Sam Illo is a doubt as he enters the return to play process, while utility back Jamie Osborne is ruled out with a pectoral injury that forced him off in the opening minutes of the Fiji game.

If Illo misses the Springboks game, Farrell has Thomas Clarkson and Tom O'Toole as back-up tight-head options with Tadhg Furlong expected to start.

Farrell will name his team to face the back-to-back world champions at 14:00 GMT on Thursday.

South Africa won last year's meeting 24-13 in Dublin but lost to France in Paris last weekend.

title: SA recall Etzebeth as Erasmus defends late changes
article_text:
South Africa record cap holder Eben Etzebeth has been recalled for Saturday's much-anticipated Nations Championship game against Ireland in Dublin.

Etzebeth, 35, missed the Springboks' win over Italy and defeat by France because of injury, but replaces Lood de Jager to earn a record-extending 148th Test cap alongside Ruan Nortje in the world champions' second row.

Cameron Hanekom is named at number eight, replacing Jasper Wiese, who is facing a possible ban after being sent off for a dangerous clear-out in the France game.

Hanekom joins captain Siya Kolisi and two-time World Rugby player of the year Pieter-Steph du Toit in the back row, with Marco van Staden replacing Hanekom on the bench.

Ox Nche, Malcolm Marx and Wilco Louw are named as the starting front row at the Aviva Stadium (16:40 GMT).

Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus also named Nche, Marx and Louw to start the France game but swapped them out for Jan-Hendrik Wessels, Gerhard Steenekamp and Thomas du Toit shortly before kick-off at the Stade de France.

Speaking to reporters on Monday, Erasmus defended that decision.

"We saw the team France had selected and looked at the players we were going to face," he said.

"We probably could have made the changes when they announced their side on Thursday, but the regulations allow you to change the team the following morning before the game.

"We thought, 'Let's get Jan-Hendrik Wessels, Thomas du Toit and Gerhard Steenekamp out there'. Maybe we'll need them next year at the World Cup, under pressure, starting a big Test match for us against one of the best scrummaging packs.

"That was the thinking behind it. We wanted to expose those guys to that pressure and give them that experience."

Erasmus added: "If people are going to keep getting upset about it, then I apologise. But I'm not apologising for doing it. I'm apologising because you're probably going to keep getting upset about it!

"If Ireland name a side on Thursday and that we didn't think they were going to play, we might make some changes."

Fly-half Manie Libbok, whose missed conversion attempt cost the Boks a draw against France, is dropped, with Canan Moodie called into the matchday squad, while Grant Williams replaces Cobus Reinach as the back-up scrum-half.

Erasmus has stuck with the backline that started in Paris. Damian Willemse, Kurt-Lee Arendse and Ethan Hooker are retained in the back three with Jesse Kriel and Damian de Allende again lining out in midfield.

Star fly-half Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu and Morne van den Berg continue their half-back partnership.

Reflecting on last week's loss, Erasmus said: "We let ourselves and the country down, and we are determined to fix the mistakes that cost us, so we'll leave no stone unturned to ensure that we play according to our standards this weekend.

"The coaches and the entire squad took a good look at ourselves over the last few days and we know what we did wrong and what we have to improve on, so we know what we have to do this week, and we'll give everything at training and on the field on the weekend."

South Africa sit second in the Nations Championship southern hemisphere standings, a point adrift of New Zealand.

A South Africa win over Ireland coupled with England beating the All Blacks (Saturday, 14:10 GMT) would be enough for Erasmus' side to seal a place in the 29 November final against the top-ranked northern hemisphere side at Twickenham.

The Springboks won 24-13 in Dublin last year, their first victory over Ireland since 2012.

South Africa: Willemse; Arendse, Kriel, De Allende, Hooker; Feinberg-Mngomezulu, Van den Berg; Nche, Marx, Louw, Etzebeth, Nortje, Kolisi (capt), PS Du Toit, Hanekom.

Replacements: Wessels, Steenekamp, T du Toit, De Jager, De Villiers, Van Staden, Williams, Moodie.

title: Lakshya aims to seal BWF World Tour final spot at Hong Kong Open
article_text:
Kowloon (Hong Kong), Nov 16 (PTI) India’s Lakshya Sen will aim to continue his rampaging run, go deep into the draw and seal his place in the season-ending BWF World Tour Finals when he begins his campaign at the Hong Kong Super 500 starting here on Tuesday.

With back-to-back titles at the Hylo Open and Kumamoto Masters Japan, the 25-year-old came out of nowhere to climb to sixth spot in the World Tour rankings and almost seal his ticket to Hangzhou, China.

However, his spot is not yet sealed, as Koki Watanabe and Kunlavut Vitidsarn are also in the race to break into the top eight and secure a place in the season finale in December.

Following his superb win over Watanabe, Sen moved ahead of the Japanese player, but it will still come down to the Hong Kong Open next week.

Lakshya has no points to defend from his runner-up finish in Hong Kong last year. Only a player’s best-14 results count, which means anything he earns in Hong Kong will replace his current lowest score of 2,220 points.

Lakshya will need to reach the semifinals in Hong Kong to be certain of his spot. However, it will also depend on how the others fare in the tournament, the final event of the qualifying window.

Lakshya opens against Lee Cheuk Yiu, while Kunlavut faces a qualifier. If both Lakshya and Kunlavut win their opening matches, they will set up a mouth-watering clash in the second round.

Watanabe is in the other half of the draw and will start against compatriot Kenta Nishimoto, meaning he can meet either of them only in the final.

“Definitely that is one thing which we will be fighting for and yes, this tournament will definitely help me get good points for that as well. Now I have one more tournament, the Hong Kong Open, so now focused on that,” Lakshya said after his win on Sunday.

Among other Indians, Kidambi Srikanth will meet seventh seed Alwi Farhan, who has already sealed his place in the season finale.

There will be a host of young Indian players in the women’s singles, with Anmol Kharb facing Japan’s fourth seed Tomoka Miyazaki, Unnati Hooda taking on eighth seed Han Yue, and compatriots Ashmita Chaliha and Isharani Baruah facing each other in their opening match.

Devika Sihag will meet Lin Hsiang Ti of Chinese Taipei, while Rakshita Ramraj will square off against Denmark’s Mia Blichfeldt.

In men’s doubles, world No. 6 Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, seeded fifth, are scheduled to face China’s Hu Ke Yuan and Lin Xiang Yi, while Hariharan Amsakarunan and MR Arjun will open against a qualifier.

Kumamoto title marks Sen’s sixth BWF tour title and his first time winning two titles in a single season. He previously won the Hylo Open 2026 title along with PV Sindhu. He now also leads the head-to-head record with Watanabe 5-3. Earlier, he lost to the Japanese at the Japan Open and the Singapore Badminton Open. With two titles in two weeks, Lakshya is sixth in line in the BWF World Tour Finals standings. The 25-year-old was 12th before the Kumamoto final, but currently ranks 11th, taking him closer to qualifying for the finals.

title: Wales international steps away from rugby at 29 in 'difficult' announcement
article_text:
Wales international Alisha Joyce has announced she is taking a break from rugby after more than a decade representing her country, with the 29-year-old deciding to step away as she reassesses her priorities.

The flanker, who won 54 caps for Wales, has informed the Welsh Rugby Union of her decision, which has been accepted by the governing body as she takes stock of her future.

Joyce has been a mainstay of the Wales squad since making her international debut against Ireland in the 2016 Six Nations and became one of the most recognisable faces in the women's game.

Her decision comes less than a year after one of the most remarkable chapters of her career, having returned to international rugby just 158 days after giving birth to her son Ralphie in November 2025.

Married to fellow Wales international Jasmine Joyce, Alisha had initially stepped away during her pregnancy but made her return to rugby after just 123 days, coming off the bench for Brython Thunder in the Celtic Challenge semi-finals.

She subsequently earned a place on the bench for Wales' clash with England in the 2026 Women's Six Nations, with her return to Test rugby becoming one of the standout stories of the championship.

Alongside her wife Jaz, she also helped document their journey into parenthood through the Vodafone-backed 'Still a Force' docuseries, which followed their decision to start a family through IVF. The series won Best Brand Partnership in Women's Sport at the 2026 ISC Awards.

In a statement, Joyce said: "This has been a difficult decision but one I have been contemplating for a while. I have loved being a professional rugby player and I wouldn’t have missed it for the world.

"It just feels like the right time to step away with my priorities having changed and having played rugby at the highest level for more than a decade.

"I always intended to return and resume my rugby career when I was first pregnant, and I am proud that I did that and hope it proves that it can be done.

"Playing for Wales has been a privilege and being part of the revolution in women’s rugby and seeing it grow as fast as it has, is something I am proud to have played a part in.

"I would like to thank everyone, teammates, coaches and staff at the WRU for the support I’ve had during my pregnancy and since being a mum and as a professional rugby player."

Wales head coach Sean Lynn paid tribute to Joyce's contribution, while making clear she would be welcome back in the international set-up.

"Alisha has been one of the most recognisable faces in women’s rugby and will be missed by her teammates, coaches and staff in the Wales set-up.

"They way she returned to Test match rugby 158 days after giving birth to Ralphie was truly inspirational to everyone.

"We respect ‘Butch’s’ decision but hope she knows the door is always open and do hope she stays involved in the game in some capacity."

WRU director of rugby and elite performance Dave Reddin added: "We all respect Alisha’s decision and appreciate how tough it would have been to make this decision.

"She has been a key figure in the Wales squad and very much a face of women’s rugby in Wales and we wish her all the best in the future."

WRU director of women's rugby Nadine Griffiths described Joyce as an inspiration to the next generation.

"Alisha has been such an inspiration to so many people as a player and a person, and I had the honour of seeing the impact she has had when I picked up the award for the docuseries ‘Still a Force’ on her and Jaz’s behalf.

"She will be one of the Welsh players who young players will reference as their hero and inspiration and will acknowledge as one of the giants of the game who showed them what can be achieved."

title: Rankings Watch: Andreeva ends year at No. 2, Andreescu continues resurgence
article_text:
The 2026 WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz season concluded last week with the FAGE WTA Finals at Indian Wells, where Mirra Andreeva was crowned champion following a dominant run through the field.

Andreeva, 19, became the youngest WTA Finals champion since a 17-year-old Maria Sharapova in 2004, and the third player in tournament history to lift the trophy on her debut without dropping a set (following Chris Evert in 1972 and Serena Williams in 2001). The 26 games that Andreeva conceded were the second-fewest since 2003, when the event switched to its current round-robin format, behind only Iga Swiatek's 20 games lost in 2023.

As a result, Andreeva climbs one place in the latest edition of the PIF WTA Rankings to end the year at a new career high of No. 2, displacing Aryna Sabalenka to No. 3. This week marks the first time that neither Sabalenka nor Iga Swiatek have featured in the Top 2 since March 2022, when Ashleigh Barty was World No. 1 and Barbora Krejcikova was World No. 2.

The only other movement in the Top 10 as a result of the WTA Finals is semifinalist Linda Noskova's climb of one place to No. 6. The Wimbledon champion ends the year as the Czech No. 1, with Karolina Muchova pushed down one spot to No. 7.

1. Elena Rybakina (+4 from No. 5 in the 2025 year-end rankings)

Last week also saw a number of players use WTA 125 and World Tennis events to put themselves in a strong year-end position.

Former US Open champion Bianca Andreescu claimed the Sopo WTA 125 title on clay in Colombia last week, defeating Elizabeth Mandlik 6-3, 6-3 in the final, to continue her resurgence at that level. In four tournaments across three continents and two surfaces over the past five weeks, the Canadian has reached four finals and collected three trophies, winning 19 of her past 20 matches.

Andreescu ended 2025 ranked No. 227 and five weeks ago, she was at No. 168. She's cut her ranking by 91 spots since then, jumping another 13 places this week from No. 100 to No. 77 -- her highest position since October 2023. Meanwhile, former No. 97 Mandlik climbs 43 places from No. 237 to No. 194 after reaching her second WTA 125 final, and first since Reus 2023.

Three high-level World Tennis tournaments also took place last week. In Brisbane, Joanna Garland collected her second W75 title in the past three months, and moves up 30 spots from No. 182 to No. 152. In Yokohama, Kyoka Okamura lifted the trophy on home soil without dropping a set, and climbs 29 places from No. 243 to No. 214. And in Chihuahua, 2025 finalist Kayla Cross went one better to take the title this year, and advances 15 places from No. 208 to No. 193.

title: Why the WTA is ready to build its own merchandise business
article_text:
The Women’s Tennis Association (WTA) is making its biggest move into the merchandise category in its 53-year history.

At last week’s WTA Finals in Indian Wells, the tour unveiled its first-ever official merchandise collaboration with Japanese entertainment company Sanrio’s Hello Kitty to create co-branded t-shirts, sweatshirts and a collectible plush. That was followed by further partnerships with women’s sports media and commerce company Togethxr and Monarch Commerce, which will launch the tour’s first online fan shop next year.

The push into consumer products comes a year after WTA Ventures, the organisation’s commercial arm, launched a refreshed brand identity for the tour as part of a wider strategy to build a lifestyle brand that has relevance beyond the sport itself.

Established in 2023 to drive new revenue into the sport, WTA Ventures has so far focused on growing the tour’s sponsorship and media rights income. Speaking to SportsPro, WTA chief brand officer Sarah Swanson said merchandise has always been part of the plan.

“We wanted to make sure first we had our brand in order,” she said. “Now, we’re looking at ways that we can take it to market outside of the traditional sponsorship assets and media rights. The consumer products space fell squarely in that plan.”

Given the history and prestige of the WTA, some might wonder why the tour hasn’t made a more concerted push into merchandise until now. More than four million spectators attended its events in 2025 and the organisation boasts nearly three million YouTube subscribers, two million followers on Instagram and 1.4 million on TikTok.

Swanson pointed out that unlike team sports, where supporters routinely show their allegiance through club merchandise, fandom in sports like tennis centres on individual athletes. That has historically left the tour with less room to capitalise on its own branded products.

One of the WTA’s priorities now is to give its longstanding fans a visible way to express their connection to women’s tennis.

“This is the first time where people who have been fans of women’s tennis for a really long time are able to show that fandom,” Swanson said.

She added that merchandise has traditionally been viewed as the bottom of the funnel: fans discover a sport, fall in love with it and eventually purchase products. However, as the WTA looks to reach new audiences, Swanson believes this dynamic can also work in reverse.

“In many cases, the product can be the top of the funnel,” she continued. “You come across a piece of merchandise that you really love and buy it, and then think, let me check out the sport that sits behind this really cool piece of merchandise.

“And I think for us, it’s going to be both ends of that.”

Given the WTA’s pioneering role in women’s sport, it seems apt that it is expanding into merchandise alongside three partners shaped by women. Hello Kitty, which debuted just one year after the WTA was founded in 1973, was created by a female designer, while Togethxr and Monarch are both women-founded businesses.

The partnership with Hello Kitty is being delivered through three of Sanrio’s existing licensees, Wild Collective, Forever Collectibles and Homage. Swanson said WTA Ventures has entered a relationship with each of those companies, which is “something that we’ll build on in the future”.

Hello Kitty is also no stranger to women’s sport, with Sanrio having previously struck partnerships with the likes of the Ladies Professional Golf Association (LPGA), all-female racing series F1 Academy and the International Cricket Council (ICC) for the 2026 Women’s T20 World Cup.

Meanwhile, the Togethxr tie-up is an expansion of an existing relationship which has seen the pair work together editorially. The latest collaboration kicked off with the launch of a women’s tennis-themed collection of the hugely popular ‘Everyone Watches Women’s Sports’ T-shirt.

“We’ve always believed the demand for women’s sports merchandise was there, but the availability, creativity and investment in the product hadn’t caught up with the audience,” Bailey Williamson, senior vice president of partnerships at Togethxr, told SportsPro.

“That’s changing, and partnerships like this are helping accelerate it.

“When you give fans something they’re genuinely excited to wear, you’re creating more than a transaction. You’re building community, driving visibility and giving people another way to show up for women’s sports.”

While Hello Kitty and Togethxr will provide further cultural relevance for the WTA and help take the tour’s brand into new spaces, Monarch Commerce will play more of an operational role, ensuring fans can buy the new products.

A subsidiary of women’s sports private equity firm Monarch Collective, the company already has partnerships with the Women’s National Basketball Association’s (WNBA) Atlanta Dream and Just Women’s Sports.

As Samantha Bushy, chief executive at Monarch Commerce, put it: “We are the feet underneath the swan, designing the product, bringing the product in, setting up the store and running the store. But for consumers, it should just look like a WTA-branded store.”

The online shop is set to launch in spring 2027, with Monarch Commerce adopting a test-and-learn approach that will allow the tour to refine its product offering as it gathers data on what resonates with fans.

The initial product range will be anchored by white-label, WTA-branded merchandise that draws heavily on the tour’s visual identity. Licensed products from Hello Kitty and Togethxr will also be available, making the store a one-stop shop for women’s tennis merch.

“It’s going to be well beyond T-shirts,” said Bushy. “It’s going to be jackets, sweatshirts, hats, visors, bags, shorts.

title: Townsend hails Scotland's defence in Australia 'arm wrestle'
article_text:
Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend hailed his team's defensive efforts after they edged past Australia in a Nations Championship "arm wrestle" at Murrayfield.

Off the back of being dismantled by New Zealand last weekend, in which they failed to score a second half point, the spotlight fell on Scotland's leaky defence.

But on a chilly and damp Edinburgh day where physicality was king, they delivered a much-needed win and showed they are capable of winning ugly.

Even so, Townsend's side didn't make it easy.

Max Jorgensen's late converted try gave the Wallabies hope, and with the clock in the red, the visitors broke from their own half.

Murrayfield held its breath, but Darcy Graham hauled Australia full-back Tom Wright into touch with a superb tackle.

"When we saw the rain half an hour before kick-off, you still hope you'll be able to move the ball," Townsend said.

"You could tell defences were coming off the line a bit quicker, knowing they could pressure the ball carrier.

"Both teams had to adjust and I thought we did that well. Defensively, that's one of the best performances I've seen in the last couple of years. Set after set we were putting them under pressure.

"We were on that edge of physicality but disciplined, hitting hard in the tackle, putting pressure on, listening to the referee, getting back onside. That makes it hard for the opposition to get into our 22m, which was a learning from last week.

"It was just constant effort. Today, we showed we can play another game, too."

Leading 12-5 at half-time, there was one eye on whether Scotland could clinch a bonus-point victory that would have both boosted their points difference and helped their chances of climbing the northern hemisphere table with Japan to come on Saturday.

However, it soon became apparent that would not be forthcoming in a match that will not live long in the memory.

"It was about winning at all costs today," former Scotland prop Peter Wright said.

"We hoped we might get something quite end-to-end, 50 points to 48, loads of tries, but to come out on the right end of a war of attrition like that, it's a good feeling.

"When you're Scottish, winning's always good. We very rarely win in style at any sport. We just want to get victories under our belt.

"It was a bad game last week so getting some momentum going into the Japan game next week was really important.

In the absence of Sione Tuipulotu, who was ruled out of playing against the country of his birth with a knee injury, Rory Darge captained Scotland and led from the front with a player-of-the-match display.

The Glasgow Warriors flanker was immense in contact and at the breakdown, and also had the presence of mind to tell Finn Russell to kick at goal instead of going to the corner in the closing stages.

The resulting three points put Scotland 10 points in front and proved to be the winning score.

Townsend praised the performance his stand-in skipper, while also pointing to a wider effort defensively.

"You know the opposition will get phases of attack and we'll have to defend. Rory with his tackling, with his effort and his post-tackle presence really helps us.

"There were a lot of other players that stood up physically. The shots that were going in, the effort going in was outstanding."

And Darge himself was heartened by how Scotland responded to the All Blacks loss.

"We were disappointed after last week's performance," he said.

"A lot of that disappointment was with the physical side of the game and we did that really well.

"It was a bit of an arm wrestle, the conditions played their part. We know they want to throw the ball around, we like to play an attacking style but today was a battle of the defences."

title: Latest 'Kilted Kiwi' in the mix for Scotland selection for Japan Test
article_text:
Scotland’s latest ‘kilted Kiwi’ could be in line for a Test debut on Saturday against Japan as Gregor Townsend plans changes to simulate scenarios his side might face at next year’s World Cup.

Glasgow full-back Josh McKay is now available to the Scotland head coach after qualifying via the residency rule this week, five years after arriving at Scotstoun in mid-November 2021.

The swashbuckling Kiwi, 29, has been a beacon of excellence and consistency for Warriors, scoring 25 tries in 85 games for the club since arriving from Canterbury.

Scotland already have stiff competition at full-back, with McKay’s Glasgow team-mates Kyle Rowe and Ollie Smith, plus another ex-Warrior in Tom Jordan, all options at No.15 alongside regular starter Blair Kinghorn.

McKay started Glasgow’s first three URC matches this term but has not played since 9 October after suffering a minor hamstring strain while warming up with the side before they faced Benetton on 30 October.

But Townsend confirmed he will be in the selection mix this week, with other squad members who have yet to feature this month – such as Smith, Duhan van der Merwe, Rory Hutchinson, Fergus Burke, Seb Stephen, Nathan McBeth, D’arcy Rae, Jonny Gray, Alex Craig, Liam McConnell and Freddy Douglas – also coming into contention.

“He [McKay] will be available,” Townsend said. “Josh hadn’t done as much since the first week of training with us because he was coming off that injury he got at Glasgow. But he was training fully Wednesday and Thursday. He’ll be one of the ones competing to start.”

The make-up of the back-three will depend on where Townsend decides to deploy the versatile Jamie Dobie, who started on the wing against New Zealand before coming off the bench to play scrum-half for the last half-hour in Sunday’s win over Australia.

With Ben White managing a knee issue, either Dobie or George Horne are likely to start at No.9 against Japan.

“Whether we consider him a nine again next week or back three, that will open up more opportunities for the back three if Jamie’s at nine,” Townsend explained. “I think he’s shown when he’s gone in there, he’s done really well.

“He came off the bench against Fiji [in July] at nine and did very well. He helped change the game and I thought he was excellent on Sunday, in a different sort of game. Jamie’s big strength is his running game, but I felt his speed and his accuracy around his passing and kicking was very good.”

Townsend admitted he had a team in mind for this weekend but would need to change it in the wake of the situation with captain Sione Tuipulotu, who is awaiting specialist advice on a knee injury which forced him to miss the Australia game.

Stafford McDowall, who was drafted onto the bench against Australia with Tom Jordan replacing Tuipulotu at 12, could potentially captain the side against Japan, as he has done in the past, although the excellent Jordan could be retained at 12 with Hutchinson also a starting midfield option, with Huw Jones likely to be rested.

It will be one of the last chances for Townsend to assess some of the players competing for the last half-dozen or so places in his 2027 World Cup squad. They are likely to be needed for either Scotland’s opening game in Australia against Uruguay in Melbourne, or their final pool game against Portugal in Brisbane before the knock-out stages.

Should Scotland fail to win their critical second pool game in Perth against Ireland, who have won their last 12 meetings and beat the Scots in the pool stages of the last two World Cups, they are likely to face a Round-of-16 encounter with France, who are expected to win Pool E. A far more favourable path into the knock-out stages is available should Scotland break their Ireland hex.

“The World Cup is now in our conversation – who could get an opportunity now that might get an opportunity in one of those pool games in the World Cup,” Townsend said.

“I know there’s still 12 months for other players to show their form, but it’s a game that we have to freshen up our team to be able to master Japan and play at the pace they’ll want to play at. They’re on their third Test match as well. They have an extra day of recovery. But I would think they’ll make changes too.

“It’s pretty tough to play three Test matches in a row with the same team. So you’ve got to rely on your depth and I’m really pleased with our depth.”

A failure to secure a try bonus-point in Sunday’s win over Australia means Scotland now have only a slim chance of overhauling Ireland or England to finish in the top three of the Nations Championship northern hemisphere standings.

They would need to beat Japan by at least 50-plus points and then hope Ireland lose by at least seven points at home to South Africa – and not pick up any match points – to finish third, while overhauling England would require a hefty defeat for Steve Borthwick’s side against New Zealand and a landslide Scottish victory over Eddie Jones’ Japan, who lost 78-15 to England on Saturday.

Even with a bonus-point win, Scotland are more likely to face whoever finishes fourth in the southern hemisphere standings on the final weekend of this month at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium. That would mean either a swift reunion with Australia, who need to beat Wales to have a chance of finishing third, or Argentina, who currently occupy third but face France in Paris on Saturday.

title: Sid Lee Sport partners with Guinness to measure the true commercial value of sports sponsorship
article_text:
Major evaluation project spans six markets and nine rights holders, moving beyond traditional media valuation to assess the business impact of Guinness’s global sponsorship portfolio.

Global sports marketing agency Sid Lee Sport, working alongside sister agency, Kepler, is undertaking a major evaluation of Guinness’s global sports sponsorship portfolio, designed to establish a clearer understanding of the commercial impact of its football and rugby partnerships.

The project covers six key markets – Great Britain, Ireland, Kenya, the United States, Indonesia and South Korea – and nine rights holders, including the Premier League, Arsenal, Aston Villa, Newcastle United, the Guinness Men’s and Women’s Six Nations and the four home rugby unions.

Sid Lee Sport and Kepler’s combined evaluation uses KIP, a custom-built, proprietary intelligence platform, to analyse three years of sales, brand and partnership data, helping isolate the incremental commercial impact of Guinness’s sponsorship investments.

The analysis goes beyond exposure, examining broadcast media value, digital reach, stadium pouring rights, fan research and experiential activation, alongside how effectively each partnership is utilised across different markets.

The evaluation aims to provide Guinness with a consistent, commercially grounded understanding of sponsorship performance across markets and partners, helping inform future investment decisions and identify opportunities to unlock greater value from its portfolio.

Mike Grumbridge, Managing Director at Sid Lee Sport, said: “The sponsorship industry continues to rely heavily on traditional metrics such as media exposure and reach to demonstrate value, but that doesn’t necessarily tell brands what their investment is delivering commercially.

“Our work with Guinness is about going much further. By combining the proprietary intelligence model of Sid Lee Sport and Kepler with deep sponsorship expertise, we’re building a clearer picture of where sponsorship creates genuine business value and how brands can unlock more of it.

“We believe this represents an important step forward in how sponsorship effectiveness is understood and measured.”

“Guinness is a brand steeped in sporting heritage and renowned for its innovation. Working with Sid Lee Sport has helped us deﬁne how we shape our brand in sport,” said Paddy Carberry, Guinness Global Marketing Manager, Head of Sport.

The Guinness project reﬂects Sid Lee Sport’s wider commitment to helping brands unlock more value from sport, bringing together world-class creativity, deep sponsorship expertise and a focus on effectiveness.

On November 10 Sid Lee Sport and Guinness will host From Pitch to Pint, a live Unofﬁcial Partner podcast at its London headquarters, bringing together representatives from the brand and agency to explore the true value of sponsorship.

The discussion will examine how brands can move beyond traditional measurement approaches and develop a more meaningful understanding of the returns generated by their partnerships. To register your interest in attending, sign up here.

This includes the likes of Tommy Hilﬁger, Visa, Guinness, UEFA, OPPO, FIFA and Lidl. title: Cricket Victoria Foundation Partners with Straight Bat Private Equity
article_text:
The Cricket Victoria Foundation has announced a new philanthropic and corporate partnership with Australian investment firm Straight Bat Private Equity to expand grassroots cricket access and community leadership initiatives across Victoria.

The agreement integrates Straight Bat into the Foundation’s flagship donor network as a Champion member of the First XI programme, while directing funding toward core community impact initiatives across the state.

Named after cricket’s hallmark principles of fair play and reliability, Straight Bat Private Equity specialises in long-term capital partnerships with established, medium-sized Australian businesses.

Under the partnership framework, Straight Bat will support the Foundation’s three primary strategic pillars, Access to the Game, Building the Future, and Strengthening Community Wellbeing, building on a previous season that engaged more than 1,000 Victorians through grassroots participation, female club leadership programmes, and the Scott Boland Indigenous Scholarship.

Cricket Victoria head of foundation, Ben Brennan, highlighted the shared values uniting corporate teamwork with community sports development.

“We’re delighted to welcome Straight Bat Private Equity as a partner of the Cricket Victoria Foundation.”

“Their focus on relationships, teamwork and supporting one another reflects our belief in cricket’s ability to bring people together and create opportunities.

“We look forward to working together and welcoming Straight Bat’s business community and their families to Junction Oval this month,” Brennan said.

Straight Bat Private Equity managing partner, Steve Gledden, emphasised the firm’s long-standing cultural connection to cricket and its commitment to backing community pathways.

“When we started Straight Bat, we signed cricket bats alongside the founders of the first businesses we backed.”

“That’s become one of our traditions. Putting our names alongside one another is our way of saying, ‘You can count on us.

“We know what a difference it makes to have someone back you, whether you’re building a business or finding your feet at a local club.

“Last season, the Foundation reached more than 1,000 Victorians.

“It helps people find a team to play for, gives women and girls the chance to lead in their clubs and, through the Scott Boland Indigenous Scholarship, supports First Nations students to study business and leadership.

“We’re proud to help the Foundation give more Victorians that kind of backing,” Gledden said.

title: Shaw and Partners Financial Services Extends Manly Warringah Sea Eagles Partnership Through 2029
article_text:
Investment and wealth management firm Shaw and Partners Financial Services has executed a three-year commercial partnership extension with National Rugby League (NRL) club the Manly Warringah Sea Eagles.

The renewed agreement takes effect from the 2027 NRL season and runs through to the end of 2029, extending an unbroken commercial alliance that first commenced in 2018.

Under the extended contract, Shaw and Partners retains prominent sleeve branding placement across both the Sea Eagles’ flagship NRL playing kit and all junior Pathways jerseys.

The multi-year renewal secures consistent commercial backing across every tier of Manly’s football operations, reinforcing corporate stability as the club prepares for its 2027 campaign at 4 Pines Park.

Shaw and Partners Financial Services CEO, Earl Evans, highlighted the firm’s long-standing commitment to the club’s heritage and talent pathways.

“We’re incredibly proud of our association with the Manly Warringah Sea Eagles and what we’ve built together since 2018.”

“Over that time, the relationship has continued to grow, and we’re pleased to reaffirm our commitment to the Club for the next three seasons.

“Manly is a club with a proud history, a passionate supporter base and a strong commitment to developing the next generation of talent.

“We are looking forward to continuing our support across both the NRL and Pathways programs,” Evans said.

Manly Warringah Sea Eagles CEO, Jason King, emphasised the importance of securing multi-year corporate support across the club’s entire football structure.

title: Classic Sportswear and NRL Extend Representative Apparel Partnership
article_text:
Australian sportswear manufacturer Classic Sportswear has officially executed a multi-year partnership extension with the National Rugby League (NRL) and the Australian Rugby League Commission (ARLC).

Announced ahead of the Rugby League World Cup Finals at Brisbane’s Suncorp Stadium, the agreement ensures Classic remains the official on-field and retail apparel partner for the Australian Kangaroos, Australian Jillaroos, Indigenous All Stars, Māori All Stars, and NRL Match Officials.

Tracing its rugby league heritage back to 1934, Classic Sportswear continues a long-standing commercial alignment that encompasses major international campaigns and retail fan-engagement programmes.

Beyond outfitting elite national and representative squads, the extended contract cements Classic’s ongoing backing of the NRL’s consumer-focused $99 jersey pricing initiative, designed to maintain retail affordability across supporter merchandise.

Classic Sportswear CEO, Ross Smart, highlighted the brand’s nine-decade heritage within rugby league and its ongoing commitment to representative pathways.

“Classic Sportswear’s commitment to Australia’s national Rugby League teams runs deep and carries through to this Rugby League World Cup, where we are thrilled to announce the continuation of our partnership with the Kangaroos, Jillaroos and the Australian Rugby League Commission.”

“Classic has proudly been there for so many great Australian moments – from the unbeaten 1986 Kangaroo Tour and World Cup triumphs in 1988 and 2000 to, more recently, Pacific Championships victories by both the Kangaroos and Jillaroos.

“Having been part of the fabric of Rugby League since 1934, we are genuine partners to the game, its clubs, players and officials.

“We look forward to carrying that proud tradition into the new term across the Kangaroos, Jillaroos, All Stars teams and Match Officials, while continuing to innovate and create for the next generation of players and fans,” Smart said.

ARLC executive chairman, Peter V’landys AM, emphasised the commercial importance of Classic’s support for affordable supporter apparel.

“Classic have been loyal partners of Rugby League for many years and I’m sure they will continue to be part of the game for many more.”

“Classic have been strong supporters of the NRL’s $99 jersey initiative. It is important for the NRL and Classic that jerseys are affordable especially in a cost of living crisis,” V’landys said.

title: "Shocked" - Springboks fans react as star is dropped for Ireland clash
article_text:
Rassie Erasmus has made five changes to his Springboks starting team for Saturday's clash against Ireland in Dublin, with Eben Etzebeth returning to the side.

The South Africa head coach has recalled the experienced lock for their penultimate Nations Championship fixture, with Etzebeth set to earn his 148th Test cap.

Ox Nche, Malcolm Marx and Wilco Louw also return to the starting line-up, while Cameron Hanekom joins captain Siya Kolisi and Pieter-Steph du Toit in the back row.

The backline remains unchanged, although Grant Williams and Canan Moodie have been added to the replacements bench.

However, one of the biggest talking points from the team announcement was the omission of Manie Libbok, who has been dropped from the matchday squad entirely, with Moodie taking his place.

Libbok came under criticism following his missed conversion against France, which would have potentially secured a draw for the Springboks. Had he successfully added the extra two points, the final result could have been very different.

Of course, the remainder of the match may also have unfolded differently, but with South Africa losing by just two points, his missed kick has attracted plenty of attention.

However, many supporters believe Libbok has been made a scapegoat and that his omission from the squad is unfair.

Reacting to the announcement, one fan wrote: "Why is Manie always the fall guy man 😢."

Others questioned why Libbok had been dropped rather than Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, who endured a difficult afternoon and was handed a 4/10 rating by RUCK.

One supporter said: "I know Manie missed a kick, but would prefer to see him starting. Let Krappies [Morne van den Berg] or Willemse kick 😉."

Another added: "I'm shocked, why Sacha? Manie dropped again"

There were also calls for Handre Pollard to return to the starting line-up, with his reputation as one of the most reliable and clutch goal-kickers in world rugby clearly still influencing supporters.

Fortunately for the Springboks, New Zealand's defeat to Wales has kept the race for top spot in the southern hemisphere table wide open, with just one point separating the two sides.

Saturday's meeting with Ireland could therefore prove decisive in determining whether Erasmus' side finish top of the southern hemisphere standings and secure a place in the Nations Championship final.

title: Henry Pollock reveals plans to switch sports for 2028 Olympics
article_text:
Henry Pollock has reaffirmed his ambition to represent Great Britain Sevens at the 2028 Olympic Games, admitting that Antoine Dupont's success in Paris has inspired him to pursue the opportunity.

The Northampton Saints and England back row has previously spoken about his interest in making the switch to sevens and has now made it clear that competing at the Olympics remains a major career goal.

Still only 21, Pollock has already enjoyed a remarkable rise through the game.

He has earned his England debut, become the youngest player to score a Six Nations try for England, toured with the British and Irish Lions last summer and helped Northampton Saints win the Gallagher PREM.

The flanker made just his second England start at the weekend, featuring at No.8 as Steve Borthwick's side secured a convincing victory over Japan.

It followed a 40-minute cameo on the wing against Australia the previous week, in which he scored two tries and showcased his positional versatility.

His growing reputation has also made him one of rugby's most recognisable young faces, with his outspoken personality attracting plenty of attention both on and off the pitch.

Pollock joined Eddie Hearn's Matchroom Talent Agency earlier this year, further highlighting his increasing profile. He is one of only two rugby players represented by the agency, alongside Scotland fly-half Finn Russell.

There had also been uncertainty surrounding his club future, but Pollock has since agreed a contract extension, first reported by RUCK, which will keep him at Franklin's Gardens until at least 2029.

The new deal could give him the opportunity to feature at both the 2027 Rugby World Cup and the 2028 Olympics.

Speaking on his YouTube channel during a Q&A session in October, Pollock was asked about his ambitions for the next few years. Understandably, next year's World Cup is currently his main priority.

"We've got the World Cup coming up next year, so that will be big. Hopefully we do really well in that tournament. After that, just see how my career goes and keep enjoying my rugby.

"That's the main thing for me, I love playing this game, I love playing this sport, I love playing in front of you guys [fans] and for me, it's just something I love to do."

However, when asked specifically about the possibility of representing Great Britain at the Olympics, the 21-year-old was equally enthusiastic.

His interest in a potential sevens switch had previously been revealed by Eddie Hearn, and Pollock confirmed that it remains something he hopes to achieve.

"Hopefully. I don't know yet how it will work but it's definitely something that I want to do in my career. Seeing what Antoine Dupont did in the last Olympics, it's definitely given me some motivation to go out and play.

"I just need to take it step-by-step and hope that it all fits in place and naturally happens. But, definitely, that's something that I'm aspiring to do."

France scrum-half Antoine Dupont famously stepped away from the 15-a-side game for several months to concentrate on sevens ahead of the Paris 2024 Olympics.

It proved an inspired decision, with France defeating two-time Olympic champions Fiji on home soil to secure the gold medal.

However, there is no guarantee that Great Britain Sevens will even qualify for the 2028 Games, having missed out on Paris 2024.

The qualification process begins this season, with four places available through the 2027 SVNS World Championship standings, six through regional qualification and the final spot to be decided by a repechage tournament in June 2028.

The United States will qualify automatically as hosts.

Great Britain's task has also become more difficult after losing their place in the eight-team top tier of SVNS.

If they do manage to secure qualification, several established 15-a-side internationals could be tempted by the opportunity to switch codes.

However, recruiting high-profile players such as Pollock would need careful consideration, particularly given the efforts of the existing squad who are working towards securing Great Britain's place at the Olympics.

title: Alzheimer’s Research UK becomes World Seniors Snooker charity partner
article_text:
Alzheimer’s Research UK has joined the World Seniors Snooker Tour as its charity partner, bringing the sport’s most recognisable veteran names behind the push for a cure for dementia.

The partnership will raise awareness of dementia and the need for research, while creating opportunities to generate funds for the charity’s work. The Tour will use its events, platforms and profile within the sport to spotlight Alzheimer’s Research UK and encourage players, fans and supporters to back the cause.

Alzheimer’s Research UK is the largest UK charity dedicated to dementia research. It funds research, challenges misconceptions and supports everyone affected by a condition that touches millions of families across the country.

Rohit Sagoo, Director at the World Seniors Snooker Tour, said, “We are absolutely delighted to welcome Alzheimer’s Research UK as our official charity partner. “Snooker is a sport that brings generations together, and we hope this partnership will allow us to make a meaningful contribution to a cause that deserves all the support it can get.”

The partnership also ties into the charity’s Think Brain Health campaign, which sets out three simple rules to help reduce dementia risk: love your heart, stay sharp and keep connected.

Zoe Dean, Senior Relationship Fundraiser at Alzheimer’s Research UK, said, “We are delighted to be the official charity partner for the World Seniors Snooker Tour. Snooker has such a passionate and engaged community, and this partnership gives us a fantastic opportunity to raise awareness of dementia, inspire people to get involved and raise vital funds for research. Playing snooker is also a great way to stay sharp and keep connected, two key messages of our Think Brain Health campaign that encourages people to take positive steps to look after their brain health.“

title: USA Eagles find their spark in Bucharest ahead of crunch Georgia test
article_text:
What a difference a week can make in sport.

For the USA Eagles, the difference between their performance against Hong Kong China and Saturday’s showing against Romania in Bucharest was night and day.

The Eagles maintained their 100% winning record in the Nations Cup and were crowned pool champions. But it was the improvement in performance that made me far happier than any trophy.

After I struggled to find positives last week, Bucharest, a happy hunting ground for the Eagles in recent history, gave USA supporters something to smile about.

Most pleasing was the confidence shown in the opening twenty minutes.

It would have been easy for Scott Lawrence’s men to retreat into their shells and adopt a risk-averse game plan with little imagination. Instead, Noah Brown’s opening try demonstrated awareness, execution and a willingness to put dangerous athletes into space.

Chicago Hounds fly-half Chris Hilsenbeck connected with a beautiful first-phase cross-field kick from a scrum, finding his Hounds teammate Brown, who showed his power and pace to finish in the corner.

The lineout was also operating with efficiency and consistency.

It was brilliant to see Provence Rugby’s Kapeli Pifeleti back in the hooker jersey. His ability to find jumpers at the front, middle and back of the lineout made an enormous difference.

Not only did it provide a platform for purposeful competitive and territorial kicking, but it also gave the Eagles opportunities to launch attacking strikes.

Their second try came from exactly that.

Clean lineout ball towards the back allowed the Eagles to attack around the tail of Romania’s defensive line. Clever decoy running opened a gap for Rufus McLean, and the former Scotland winger showed his pace to finish under the posts.

Two set pieces. Two first-phase attacks. Two tries.

It’s been a while since I’ve seen that from a USA Eagles side.

Lawrence’s men maintained the physical edge shown in patches against Hong Kong China, something clearly central to their game model. But one-off carries will only get you so far.

This time, there was more variation, movement and interplay between forwards and backs.

Hilsenbeck delivered a far more controlled performance, undoubtedly helped by the platform provided by his forwards. The movement and execution leading to Perry Mayo’s try in the corner were described perfectly by one Eagles supporter who messaged me during the game: “Smooth.”

Not a word frequently associated with recent Eagles performances.

It was refreshing to see the dangerous back three given opportunities to showcase their abilities. Unsurprisingly, all three scored, with McLean grabbing a double.

Pifeleti’s return was complemented by Stade Français loosehead Jack Iscaro and Montauban back-rower Nafi Ma’afu, both of whom impressed.

You could see what wearing the USA jersey meant to Iscaro. When Oscar Lennon launched a long-distance box kick midway through the first half, it was ‘Big Red’ who led the chase, bringing down the Romanian receiver before he could go anywhere.

That intensity continued as the Eagles ran in seven tries and accumulated 53 points. Hilsenbeck’s boot, so vital against Hong Kong China, missed only one conversion and ended the game with a personal tally of 13 points.

Romania were undoubtedly disappointing, particularly after pushing Tonga close the previous week. But much of that was down to the Eagles.

Two Romanian tries came from driving mauls, exposing defensive vulnerabilities despite the Eagles’ own attacking maul proving so effective the previous week.

The kicking game was generally more purposeful, particularly from Lennon, but there were moments when I found myself asking: Why?

On two occasions, once in each half, the Eagles opted for contestable box kicks roughly 30 metres from Romania’s tryline.

It felt like searching for a rabbit-out-of-the-hat moment when they had already demonstrated an ability to retain possession, build phases and even force Romanian penalties at the breakdown.

Captain Jason Damm praised the team’s commitment to their “game model” afterwards.

My question is whether those kicks were part of that model or moments when the Eagles lost faith in their ability to attack with ball in hand.

There will certainly be work-ons ahead of their toughest Nations Cup challenge against Georgia in Tbilisi next Saturday.

Discipline remains a major concern. The Eagles conceded 15 penalties, with 12 coming inside their own half. A side of Georgia’s quality will punish that generosity.

Nevertheless, there was considerably more to celebrate than criticise.

Damm produced an assured captain’s performance, getting through an enormous amount of work, particularly in the second half.

As the Eagles tightened their attacking execution inside Romania’s 22, they demonstrated both patience and power. Damm benefited from one close-range forward effort, while Nathan Den Hoedt added another.

It was a stark contrast to the previous week, when opportunities inside the opposition 22 were squandered through turnovers in contact, poorly judged offloads and inaccurate passing.

And that was perhaps the most encouraging aspect of this victory.

The Eagles had clearly learned their lessons and, more importantly, put them into practice.

There is certainly no questioning the players’ desire on either side of the ball.

In the 64th minute, Hilsenbeck launched a towering kick that McLean competed for brilliantly. Eagles jerseys flooded around the contest, collecting the loose ball and creating the opportunity for Tavite Lopeti to score.

Four minutes later, despite leading by more than 30 points, Brown and Lennon worked tirelessly to get across and make a try-saving tackle on powerful Romanian winger Fonovai Tangimana.

They demonstrate a cohesive, proud culture within this Eagles squad, one that is clearly determined to improve and become competitive ahead of next year’s Rugby World Cup.

title: Pink pony club and pre-match parties: How women's rugby is reinventing matchday hospitality
article_text:
Premiership Women’s Rugby is on the march. We all know that. Season four is round the corner and there’s a shiny new title sponsor this year in the Chinese car brand JAECOO.

Ticket sales are up [rising by 23% last season], broadcast visibility and social media presence likewise. While the continued success and popularity of the Red Roses serves testimony to the strength of the PWR. Because where do the best players from the best team in the world play? That’s right.

A new metric that will be worth keeping an eye on this season – and indeed sampling for yourself should you get the chance – is hospitality at PWR matches.

Hospitality in the women’s game has so far been the preserve of England matches at Allianz Stadium, where sales have increased 147.5% since the first standalone Red Roses match at Twickenham versus France in 2023.

Now PWR clubs are getting in on the act. Last season both Sale Sharks and Exeter Chiefs sold out when hosting pre-match hospitality functions for fans. Exeter intend to double their events this season whilst Sale are aiming to replicate their success with another two sell-outs. Some clubs, such as Saracens, open their corporate boxes for women’s games but haven’t yet taken the plunge with a separate hospitality offering for ticket-paying fans. But it won’t be long. Loughborough Lightning for example intend to make their hospitality debut around a few targeted fixtures this season.

While this is exciting news for fans, it’s equally exciting for the business behind women’s rugby. Hospitality being an area that clubs can only afford to look at once they feel their general admission ticket sales are heading in the right direction and that the matchday experience for those fans is right. Conversely, hospitality will be the first area to show a decline in sales if fans are dissatisfied with the performance on the pitch. It’s a bellwether for fan interest. The canary in the mine.

But getting hospitality right can be extremely lucrative. Sports events with established hospitality offerings can charge anywhere between two and 10 times the amount of a general admission ticket, a very handy extra line on the balance sheet.

For example, at the recent England v New Zealand match at Allianz Stadium, for £310, Red Roses fans could attend a ‘suite-to-seat’ brunch with a buffet and an all-inclusive bar open from around four hours before kick-off with a pre-match Q&A hosted by The Good, The Scaz & The Rugby podcast with guests including Abbie Ward, Amy Rule and Katy Daley-McLean. With regular tickets averaging out at £25 for adults and £5 for juniors, the 250 fans who paid for this hospitality package provided the same revenue as selling an extra 5,000 tickets to the match, if you assume an equal number of adult and junior tickets were sold on the day.

Of course, no PWR club right now can dream of emulating those kind of numbers. And refreshingly, no-one is trying to. Instead, hospitality in PWR is focused on creating an extra way to bring fans together, without asking them to fork out the kind of cash you would need to at Allianz Stadium or for hospitality at a men’s match in the Gallagher PREM.

Testament to this is Exeter, who held their first hospitality event last season. Chiefs charged £38 on top of an £12 match ticket for the game versus Sale Sharks. They sold 179 tickets, which filled the pitch-facing suite they hosted it in. For that price, guests received a drink on arrival as well as their own drinks tray, a mezze buffet and a Q&A hosted by Chiefs players Gabby Cantorna and Edel McMahon. But where the event really distinguished itself was with its theme.

“We went for ‘an Ibiza, chilled, pink pony-club vibe,’ explained Caroline Moore, Exeter’s former head of communications. “We had dance music, there were heart-shaped sunglasses and complimentary hairclips and paper tissue garlands on the table.

“It came from thinking ‘we can do something different’ but also fans were asking us for an upgrade on the match-day experience.

“We’ve done a shepherd’s pie, a pint or a glass of wine before but it wasn’t particularly well attended. We wanted to move it away from the traditional men’s offering.

“It wasn’t all women. If you look at the crowd that came, it was a blend of ages as well.

“We wanted to make it a bit more interactive so they did a quiz where all the questions were based around the players. But it was mainly them [Gabby and Edel] chatting, it was more relaxed and they will have known almost everybody in the room.

“We will definitely do it again. We made money on it and we’ll have at least two this season coming, one in winter and one in summer.

“We got some lovely comments from supporters, who were just grateful that the women were getting the same treatment.”

Admirers of this more relaxed atmosphere include the Red Roses themselves, who will look to follow suit and open-up another part of Allianz Stadium at England’s home match versus France on Saturday 15 May next year.

Plans are still taking shape but the rooftop vibes of the British Airways Rose Garden are being lined up to host fans in a party atmosphere with live music and pizzas from wood-fired ovens.

The success of any sports hospitality offering is heavily linked with the success of the team on the field and how enjoyable it is to watch them. Right now the Red Roses and the vast majority of PWR clubs are providing entertainment aplenty on the field and the brave new world of hospitality at women’s rugby is riding the crest of that wave.

title: WTA chair Valerie Camillo says the Jessica Pegula-Mirra Andreeva incident at Indian Wells was 'not bad for viewership'
article_text:
WTA chief Valerie Camillo says private comments made by Jessica Pegula about Mirra Andreeva being overheard on a YouTube livestream is "not bad for viewership".

Camillo personally apologised to Pegula, describing the broadcast of on-court conversations during a practice session at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells as "regrettable and unacceptable".

The Tour, who operated the livestream, had intended for the microphones to capture ambient sounds from the court but failed to inform participants.

A broadcast showed the American in conversation with her coach Mark Knowles, calling the 19-year-old a "diva" and saying she has lost respect for Andreeva's coach Conchita Martinez for not calling out her behaviour.

"Someone actually asked me if we planned it or did it on purpose to draw attention to the event," Camillo told Sky Sports' lead tennis commentator, Jonathan Overend.

"I wish that we were so crafty and strategic but we can't put ourselves in any situation where we put our athletes at risk. Our number one objective as a member services organisation for our players is to protect our players.

"What Jess said is competitive banter. I don't think there was anything particularly salacious in it. But having mics lying around that aren't being properly managed is not how the WTA expects to execute and operate.

"It created a viral moment. It created a lot of dialogue. But that's not intentional and not something you should expect to see us doing in the future.

"I've had this conversation here that I come from a variety of different sports. Before joining the WTA, I exclusively worked in male sports. I worked at the NBA and majorly baseball and it's quite common for there to be competitive banter that is brought into the forefront.

"It's up to the athletes for what they feel comfortable with and what they don't. But a little drama isn't bad for ticket sales.

"It's not bad for viewership. It's not bad for commentary. That's just a reality."

Andreeva laughed off the hot mic moment and went on to defeat Pegula 6-3 6-4 on Saturday, in a match that gained an extra layer of intrigue to reach the WTA Finals title match.

She concluded a stunning week with a second victory over Elina Svitolina to win the season-ending tournament.

The WTA was forced to replace the venue for the season-ending event from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, in July, which represented a major financial setback for the governing body.

The deal with the Saudi Tennis Federation (STF) included record prize money over a three-year period, but the ongoing tension between Iran and the United States made planning for the Finals more challenging, eventually forcing the tournament to move to Indian Wells in California.

The body is projecting operating losses of £17.3m ($23m) for 2026 and expects to hold roughly £11.3m ($15m) in cash by the end of the year, according to The Telegraph. Camillo remains confident of finding extra revenue streams through in-house media rights and sponsorship growth to create financial stability.

"Our ambition for the WTA Finals is equal prize money [with the men's tour]. That's our ambition, just as we expected of the Grand Slams. All of our combined 1000 events will have equal prize money in 2027," she said.

"We've been building fandom. We've been operating globally. We've been creating superstar athletes through our platform for many, many decades, and so the athletes have the opportunity not to just earn on the court, but also to control their own brands and monetise that off the court.

"WTA intends to remain in its position as number one in the hearts and minds of fans, in the mindset and investment of our sponsors, and we want to be building an even greater platform on which our great athletes can compete, not only one that they can enjoy from the ferocity of the crowd, but also one that enables them to maximise their financial opportunity to the best of our ability."

One of the WTA revenue streams comes from selling data, match data, court feeds to data companies with the betting industry a large part of that.

British tennis star Jodie Burrage called on social media platforms to hold people accountable for sending death threats and abuse.

Burrage, who was playing her first WTA Tour match since Wimbledon last summer, received death threats and online abuse following a first-round defeat at a tournament in India.

The 27-year-old shared a raft of abusive messages sent to her Instagram account. Alongside the video, Burrage wrote: "Nice welcome back to the tour. I remember why I left."

Camillo said: "The complexity of official data to these partners is sort of an industry inside thing. But the reality is that through having official partnerships, you actually can have more integrity and controls.

"If you don't have relationships with these variety of platforms, you can turn into a little bit of the wild, wild west. It's not to say that there isn't a financial element to these relationships. That would be disingenuous. Of course there is. But it does also enable us to have a partnership that leads to better controls."
