title: News: NHL media rights, Paramount-WBD, Angels and more
article_text:
The NHL has reportedly approached ESPN and TNT Sports about media rights renewals; Paramount has updated aspects of its hostile tender offer for Warner Bros. Discovery; and in-market streaming of Los Angeles Angels broadcasts will take place through the MLB DTC platform. Plus news on ESPN, Netflix, CBS-UFC and Fubo.

NHL commissioner Gary Bettman is said to have approached ESPN and TNT Sports about expediting their media rights negotiations, according to John Ourand of Puck Tuesday night. Ourand, who reported the same about the PGA Tour, wrote that the networks do not appear poised to negotiate new deals “until they know how much the NFL will ask for.” The NFL currently receives a reported sum of more than $11 billion annually for its media rights.

The NHL’s U.S. media rights deals, which are reportedly worth a combined $625 million, are not due to expire until after the 2028 season. But with the NFL widely expected to move up its media rights negotiations, leagues are reportedly looking to rush to the negotiating table while the networks still have money to spend.

TNT Sports lost its domestic NBA media rights package last year, but has in recent years acquired French Open tennis, NASCAR and — via sublicense — College Football Playoff games, among other properties. ESPN has committed billions in new rights and renewals since reacquiring NHL rights in March 2021 after a 17-year hiatus.

The NHL last year signed a 12-year media rights extension with Rogers Communications in Canada worth $11 billion CDN, but it does not begin until the 2026-27 season. Between the United States and Canada, the league will bring in reported media revenue of more than $1.2 billion USD per year for the two seasons those deals overlap.

Paramount on Tuesday updated its hostile tender offer for all of Warner Bros. Discovery to cover the $2.8 billion termination fee WBD would need to pay to get out of its commitment with Netflix, and add a $0.25/share “ticking fee” to WBD shareholders for every quarter the deal is not closed. The latter equates to approximately $650 million in cash value that would be distributed among WBD shareholders per quarter. Paramount again expressed confidence in quickly receiving the necessary regulatory approvals for the proposed transaction, which the company first initiated with a series of unsolicited bids starting last fall.

Paramount had previously sweetened its deal by raising the reverse termination fee to $5.8 billion, which is equivalent to the Netflix figure. Either of these suitors would need to compensate WBD with this fee if their pact does not receive regulatory approval. In its “enhanced” tender offer, Paramount claimed it would “fully reimburse” WBD for the potential $1.5 billion cost affiliated with not completing debt refinancing. The company said this payment would not reduce the reverse termination fee.

Paramount, which extended the expiration date for its offer by 10 days to March 2, has secured $43.6 billion in equity commitments coming from both the Ellison family and RedBird Capital Partners, including an “irrevocable personal guarantee” from Larry Ellison. Paramount also has $54 billion in debt commitments from Apollo, Bank of America and Citigroup. Moreover, Paramount said its financing sources would extend the maturity on a $15 billion bridge loan or that the company would “permit WBD to structure permanent financing in any way it chooses so long as the debt is redeemable at a commercially reasonable cost.”

Paramount has continued to argue that its bid is “superior” to the Netflix agreement, claiming the latter is operating off a sliding scale based on the amount of debt to be carried by Discovery Global. WBD disclosed that Discovery Global would carry $17 billion of debt “as of June 30, 2026” with a goal to reduce that number to $16.1 billion by year’s end. Since WBD is able to determine the amount of debt Discovery will hold prior to pro rata common stock distribution, a “debt adjustment mechanism” in the Netflix deal could potentially reduce its value. WBD confirmed receipt of Paramount’s offer, which its board will review.

The Los Angeles Angels on Tuesday joined the list of 21 Major League Baseball teams whose games will be distributed digitally via the league’s in-house direct-to-consumer platform, but it remains to be seen whether the team’s games will be produced by the league. The Angels are co-owners of the FanDuel Sports Network West RSN and are “contemplating buying out Main Street to launch their own network,” per a report by Mike Mazzeo of Sports Business Journal. Mazzeo cited sources who explained that the team has not ruled out launching a linear network this season or in the future, which could also include Los Angeles Kings NHL games.

While the majority of teams are working with MLB on the distribution of their games, not all of them are utilizing the league for production. At the moment, MLB is slated to produce live game broadcasts for the five teams it worked with last season (Diamondbacks, Guardians, Rockies, Twins, Padres) in addition to eight teams previously part of the Main Street Sports Group portfolio (Reds, Tigers, Royals, Marlins, Brewers, Cardinals, Rays, Nationals). The Seattle Mariners organization is also working with the league on production and distribution of local games after shutting down ROOT Sports Northwest last year.

For the 14 teams whose games are being both produced and distributed by MLB, the in-market streaming price is $20/month and $100 for the season. While the Angels have not announced their production arrangements for the upcoming season, the pricing is the same. MLB is also distributing local games televised on RSNs for six teams this season as well (Athletics, Orioles, Dodgers, Mets, Phillies, Giants). The pricing for these packages differs by market, and some of the solutions also include access to other programming from the applicable RSN.

title: Brady Rush hopes to bring Northland’s fairytale NPC success to SVNS
article_text:
All Blacks Sevens veteran Brady Rush is hoping to transfer Northland’s NPC success into the upcoming 2026/2027 HSBC SVNS Series.

Northland were the fairytale of the 50th NPC, winning the Ranfurly Shield for the first time since 1979 and later making their first final. They led 21-10 at halftime before succumbing to defending champions and 16-time winners Canterbury in Christchurch.

Rush started 10 games on the wing and scored four tries. Two came in a 40-14 win against Manawatu, and the others in the successful 34-17 defence of the Ranfurly Shield against Waikato and the 26-21 quarter-final victory against Tasman.

“It still feels a little surreal, what we’ve done,” Rush told RugbyPass.

“It was special for the community to come together as it did. We hadn’t won the Shield since the days of the Going brothers. Seeing what that win meant to that generation, and inspiring a new generation, are forever memories.

“After we beat Canterbury to win the Shield, the airport was packed out. Then we went on a road trip where we were treated like rockstars.

“We’ve been building over the last couple of years with a core group of boys and growing ambition. Ryan Martin is a bloody wizard, bro. Coming up North and embracing the culture and community straight away won the boys’ respect. As a coach, his detail and knowledge are second to none. Add legends Ross Wright and Robbie Abel, and from the first camp I thought, Bro, this is going to be a pretty cool season.”

Northland’s 36-12 dismantling of Canterbury on August 20 was their first win over Canterbury since 1999 and their first in Christchurch since 1987. Canterbury also suffered their heaviest home defeat since 2014. Brady’s brother Rob Rush scored two tries. He’s recovering strongly from a knee injury.

Northland repelled Shield challenges from Tasman (20-10) and Waikato (34-17) before losing to 13th-placed Counties Manukau 22-19 in their last home game of the regular season. It was a setback that could have derailed their season but instead had a mobilising effect.

“We didn’t take our chances in the Counties game, but it was cool to see a small Union like them win. Similar to us, they had parades, a packed stadium and an awesome buzz,” Rush said.

“Our goal at the start of the season was to make the final and win it. The Shield was a bonus. When we lost the Shield, it was easy to bounce back. We had a chip on our shoulder and bigger fish to fry.”

Northland rallied to beat Southland (28-14), Tasman (26-21) and Otago (38-19) to make the NPC final against Canterbury. Rush rues the defeat to the 43-24 defeat in the decider.

“It was going so well at halftime. Canterbury are a bloody good team and showed it on the day. Once they got momentum, the crowd got stuck in and they were hard to stop. I can’t put my finger on a single moment we lost, just a culmination of small moments.”

The All Blacks Sevens experienced a similar rollercoaster of emotions in HSBC SVNS 2025/2026. After winning the Dubai Sevens first up, they failed to win another title, slipping to fourth in the league standings.

In the trilogy of Grand Final tournaments, New Zealand lifted to second, narrowly losing a Cup final thriller to hosts France in Bordeaux.

“It’s a hard comp, eight teams. Anyone can beat anyone on their day,” Rush said.

“We had a lot of injuries last year that didn’t help, but we definitely changed a few things at home around preparation that helped us improve. Young fellas like Riely Williams, Fletcher Morgan and Jayden Keelan really grew during the season.

“This year is a fresh start. We’ve got a new coaching group and promising young players coming through like Grady Forbes and Nathan Salmon from Northland. Hopefully they can bring some of the Taniwha buzz.”

This weekend at the Ignite Sevens in Mount Maunganui, a New Zealand Development side that will make up most of the All Blacks Sevens had a three-match series with Samoa and Fiji.

Two tries from Brayden Neilson secured an initial 12-12 draw against Fiji, who were then beaten 12-7 and 7-5 in the next two games. Sprightly Jayden Keelan scored a crucial try in each contest.

Northland duo Scott Gregory and Nathan Salmon scored in a first-up 14-5 win against Samoa, which improved to 31-5 in the next match, with Keelan again among the scorers alongside stalwarts Regan Ware and Andrew Knewstubb.

Samoa would have the last say with a 24-17 win. Beast Taunuu Niulevaea was a handful with two tries. Salmon, Riley Williams and Joe Webber scored for New Zealand.

The Emirates Dubai 7s 2026 takes place from November 27–29 at The Sevens Stadium in Dubai. New Zealand have won the cup title six times. The current league and Grand Final champions, South Africa, are the most prolific winners, with 11 titles since 1999.

title: New World Rugby rankings published as Wales save Springboks in dramatic 18 hours
article_text:
Wales' historic victory over New Zealand has seen them move up to ninth in the world rankings and had a huge impact at the very top of the global order after a dramatic 18 hours.

The 35-28 win over the All Blacks also saw world champions South Africa regain first place after they had temporarily dropped to second following their 21-19 defeat by France in Paris on Friday night. It also resurrected the Springboks' hopes of winning the Nations Championship after they thought it was over for them.

Wales gained the highest amount of rankings points on the weekend (+2.00) and will rise further up the rankings if they can beat Australia at the Principality Stadium this Saturday.

France also moved into the top three in the world rankings following their stunning victory on Friday night with New Zealand in second place.

Despite Ireland's 43-15 hammering of Fiji at the Aviva Stadium on Saturday night, Ireland drop down to fourth place behind France.

Defeat for Fiji saw them overtaken by Wales and Jake White's side now sit in tenth place.

France are now very close to the top two on 89.09 points with New Zealand on 90.65 and South Africa on 91.53 in first place.

Scotland's narrow 15-12 win over Australia at Murrayfield on Sunday saw Gregor Townsend's men gain 0.87 ranking points but they remain in sixth place with the Wallabies in seventh.

Argentina gained 0.47 points after their 19-14 win over Italy but they remain in eight place one position above Wales.

The Azzurri have dropped out of the top 10 to 11th place.

title: Rassie Erasmus calls for Ireland star to be banned ahead of Springboks showdown
article_text:
Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus has called for Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast to face punishment over his controversial tackle against Fiji, insisting the incident deserved a red card.

The 23-year-old has now been cited following Ireland's 43-15 Nations Championship victory over Fiji, leaving him in danger of missing Saturday's showdown with South Africa.

Prendergast is accused of making an illegal hip-drop tackle on Fiji captain Peceli Yato during the first half in Dublin.

The incident went unpunished during the match, but the Ireland playmaker now faces a disciplinary process.

And Erasmus has made his feelings perfectly clear.

Despite believing the tackle deserved a red card, the Springboks boss suspects Prendergast will be available to face his side.

"We are in the northern hemisphere. I think there is going to be a technicality and he is going to play," Erasmus said.

The South African coach revealed that World Rugby had recently spent hours discussing dangerous tackling techniques with international coaches.

"I think the hip-drop tackle was terrible, in my opinion, compared to where we were at the World Rugby meetings," he said.

"We all thought it's an immediate red card. Everybody watched the game live because that's exactly what they said the hip-drop tackle is."

title: ATP Finals 2026 Day 1 Recap
article_text:
The 2026 ATP Finals got underway in Turin on Sunday, with Alexander Zverev and Ben Shelton both making winning starts in the John McEnroe Group.

World No. 1 Zverev eased past debutant Rafael Jodar in straight sets, while Shelton had to work considerably harder to overcome Arthur Fils in three, recording his first-ever match win at the year-end championships.

Neither match produced a major surprise, but Shelton’s victory sets up a clash with Zverev on Tuesday. Here’s a look at Sunday’s results, match stats and highlights, plus the schedule for Day 2, when Carlos Alcaraz begins his campaign against Frances Tiafoe.

Alexander Zverev (1) def. Rafael Jodar (8) 6-4 6-4

Alexander Zverev got his 2026 ATP Finals campaign off to a winning start on Sunday, defeating debutant Rafael Jodar 6-4, 6-4 in the opening match of the John McEnroe Group.

Zverev has been all over social media again this weekend after his ex-girlfriend filed a new civil lawsuit seeking injunctive monetary relief, claiming he made misleading statements about the legal outcomes of her case against him, which was settled in 2024.

It is, of course, more farcical stuff from Patea, and I am not sure where she got the idea from. Is she skint and needs a new handbag, are lawyers thinking they have a chance to make some cash, or will someone in the tennis article-writing fraternity with an axe to grind have spurred her on?

Back on court, Sascha was largely untroubled by the 20-year-old Spaniard, using his serve and backhand to finish in straight sets.

Jodar put up some resistance early on, saving two break points before Zverev eventually broke at 3-3 with a superb backhand winner down the line.

The German wobbled when serving for the set, falling 15-40 behind, but responded with two aces and two unreturned serves to close it out. His first-serve percentage in the opening set was an impressive 88%, with no double faults.

The second set followed a similar pattern. Jodar showed flashes of the tennis that has propelled him to the season-ending championships, but Zverev was too solid, particularly from the baseline.

Zverev played a businesslike game; his serve clicked, he looked comfortable throughout, and he will be pleased to get his first win on the board without expending too much energy.

Ben Shelton def. Arthur Fils 6-2, 3-6, 6-3

Ben Shelton secured his first-ever ATP Finals match win on Sunday evening, defeating Arthur Fils 6-2, 3-6, 6-3 in a reasonably fun match.

The American raced through the opening set with big hitting from both wings as Fils struggled to get a foothold, with Shelton dominating behind his serve and not facing a single break point.

However, the Frenchman found some success in the second set, extending the rallies and mixing up the pace to disrupt Shelton’s rhythm. He secured the decisive break in the eighth game before saving two break points to serve out the set.

Shelton regained control early in the decider, breaking in the second game to forge a lead he wouldn’t relinquish. He faced one sketchy break point while serving for the match at 5-3, but two huge aces helped him escape trouble before closing out the victory in one hour and 58 minutes.

The match also marked Juan Carlos Ferrero’s first appearance in Shelton’s coaching box, alongside his father Bryan, and I thought Ben played decently, especially on the backhand side for a change. Fils too played one of his better matches of late after struggling since Cincinnati.

The two opening-day winners are set to meet on Tuesday in what should be an interesting contest, particularly given Shelton’s serving ability on the quick indoor courts.

title: Rory McIlroy, Scottie Scheffler headline teams for Golf Channel Games
article_text:
Rory McIlroy and Scottie Scheffler once again will headline the team rosters at the Optum Golf Channel Games, which debuted in 2025 and will be held at Trump National Golf Club Jupiter.

The event will be contested on Wednesday, Dec. 16, airing live in primetime on Golf Channel and USA Network.

Tickets are on sale at thegolfchannelgames.com and at TickPick.com.

Team Rory will include 2022 U.S. Open Champion Matt Fitzpatrick, four-time PGA Tour winner Si Woo Kim and four-time DP World Tour winner Haotong Li, who is returning to Team Rory for the 2026 competition.

Team Scottie, which won last year's inaugural Optum Golf Channel Games, will feature Chris Gotterup, a five-time PGA Tour winner including three wins in 2026, three-time PGA Tour winner Michael Brennan and 2026 PGA Tour rookie standout and Tour winner Jackson Koivun.

"The inaugural Optum Golf Channel Games proved that a unique format showcasing the best players in the world under the pressure of a running clock produces a kind of energy we don't normally see in our sport," said Tom Knapp, Golf Channel EVP and GM. "That energy translated to the viewers at home and we're excited to build off of last year's momentum with this group of elite golfers, leaning into what worked well last year and implementing some new challenges this year."

World No. 1 Scheffler and No. 2 McIlroy will be leading their teams through the rapid-fire golf competition, which will feature challenges such as the Team Relay and 14-Club Challenge, as well as new challenges for the 2026 competitors.

- Six of the top 20 players in the Official World Golf Rankings: Scheffler (No. 1), McIlroy (2), Fitzpatrick (3), Gotterup (8), Kim (14) and Brennan (20).

- Three Major Champions: Scheffler, McIlroy, Fitzpatrick.

Harlequins land highly rated Eagles playmaker for new PWR campaign
article_text:
USA Women’s Eagles back Nina Mason has signed for Harlequins for the 2026/27 JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby campaign.

Mason made her Test debut for the Eagles in September, as the USA completed a 19-point turnaround to win in Dublin, and then started four international fixtures in a row to conclude WXV Global Series.

Two of those starts resulted in back-to-back victories against Italy in Texas and Tennessee. Mason also started in the Eagles’ 55-12 loss to the Red Roses at the end of October.

Mason said: “I’m so excited for the opportunity to experience rugby in England and be a part of such a great team. I’m looking forward to this next chapter with Harlequins Women and linking up with such a talented squad of players.”

Mason arrives in West London as a highly regarded prospect. During her time at Life University she was a standout performer as the team won the CRAA Division I 15s title and USA Rugby Division I Club 15s National Championship in 2026. In April, the team also won the CRAA Premier Division 7s National Championship.

Capable of playing fly-half or centre, Mason forged a formidable midfield partnership with World Rugby Women’s 15s Breakthrough Player of the Year nominee and university teammate Bella Vogel in WXV Global Series.

She is the latest arrival at the Twickenham Stoop, who have also recruited England internationals Marlie Packer and Rosie Galligan, along with Wales’ Sisilia Tuipulotu and Italy’s Sara Mannini.

Ross Chisholm, Harlequins head coach, said: “We’re excited for Nina to join us here at Harlequins. She can play in multiple positions across the backline and has shown a lot of promise in the recent WXV Series for the USA.

“She is a player who has a great feel for the game and ability to play in a number of different ways.

“She is a young player with a lot of talent and we’re looking forward to seeing what she can bring to our environment.”
